newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The pro-Beijing Federation of Trade Unions has urged the banning of Chinese Communist Party funding for local political groups.

-- APPLE DAILY -- A U.S. agency was forced to stop sponsoring a Hong Kong legislators' exchange programme because two of those taking part were also members of the China-backed provisional legislature.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng said Hong Kong was stable and prosperous and that a smooth transition from British rule was guaranteed.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- China-related shares prices fell because of rumours that Chinese economic tsar Zhu Rongji thought the stock market had surged too high.
-- Executive Councillors have proposed that the land reserve fund should continue to be managed by its current secretariat but that its main use should be to protect the Hong Kong dollar.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Bank of China group was to further cement its position as one of the most influential institutions in the region by consolidating its non-retail banking activities.
-- Red chip China Overseas Land & Investment planned to invest more than HK$2.8 billion in one industrial project and four residential projects on the mainland, marking a new wave of expansion.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin was poised to introduce a new theory of "benevolent authoritarianism" to underpin his rule over China after the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

-- Bitter wrangling between local and expatriate officials on localisation measures triggered cross-party concerns over eroding civil service morale in the crucial weeks before the handover to Chinese rule.
